## Summary
Fixes a Claude CLI `/usage` parsing bug where CodexBar reports:

```text
Could not parse Claude usage: Claude CLI usage endpoint is rate limited right now. Please try again later.
```

even though Claude Code rendered valid session and weekly usage data.

## What happened
CodexBar drives Claude Code in a PTY and sends `/usage`. In the reported case, the captured panel contained valid quota data:

```text
Current session
3% used

Current week (all models)
11% used
```

but later in the same panel Claude also rendered a non-fatal secondary notice:

```text
Per-model breakdown unavailable (rate limited -- try again in a moment)
```

- Treat Claude CLI rate-limit text as fatal only when no usable `Current session` quota value was rendered.
- Continue parsing session/week usage when only a secondary section, such as per-model breakdown, is rate limited.
- Add a regression test covering valid session/week data plus a secondary rate-limit notice.

target.title: fix(memory): bound qmd taskkill cleanup
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

QMD timeout, abort, and availability cleanup used synchronous `taskkill.exe` calls on Windows. A stalled system utility could block the Node event loop after the QMD operation had already reached its own deadline, delaying command settlement and gateway work indefinitely.

## Why This Change Was Made

Windows process-tree cleanup now launches `taskkill.exe` asynchronously and settles its cleanup attempt after five seconds without waiting for the utility to exit. The timed-out helper is terminated and detached, while the retained QMD child handle remains the final fallback.

The cleanup also rechecks the QMD child's authoritative `exitCode` and `signalCode` before forced escalation or direct kill. This avoids retrying a reusable PID after QMD exits while the asynchronous taskkill attempt is in flight. A timeout result is fixed before `kill()` runs so a synchronous child-process error cannot incorrectly trigger a second `/F` attempt.

## User Impact

On Windows, QMD operations now settle at their own timeout or abort deadline even if `taskkill.exe` stalls, so cleanup no longer blocks the gateway event loop. Normal graceful-to-forced tree cleanup remains intact for fast failures, and exited QMD processes are not targeted again by PID.

## Evidence

- Node 24.15.0: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/qmd-process.test.ts` (27/27 passed)
- Node 24.15.0: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/qmd-process.real.test.ts` (2/2 passed)
- Regression coverage verifies heartbeat responsiveness during a stalled taskkill, five-second helper settlement, retained-handle fallback, synchronous kill errors, late taskkill events, and QMD exit before retry
- `oxfmt --check packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/qmd-process.ts packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/qmd-process.test.ts`
- Targeted `oxlint` on both changed files
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`
- Node 24 child-process source/types and Bun child-process compatibility were inspected for `spawn`, exit state, `kill`, and `unref` behavior
- Two-pass independent adversarial review found and then cleared the timeout-result and stale-PID races; the final code review had no actionable finding

Proof gap: no Windows machine capable of deliberately stalling `taskkill.exe` was available in this session. The focused tests exercise the exact asynchronous OpenClaw path and event-loop behavior; GitHub CI remains the clean-environment gate.

With the vitest whales gone (top job 187s), the measured wall of a canonical main run (11.5 min, run 29592647843) is dominated by everything *around* the tests:

Closes #110065

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users setting `"enabled": false` under `agents.defaults.compaction` in `openclaw.json` would have their entire config rejected (`agents.defaults.compaction: Invalid input`) when running any gateway command. The session runtime already reads `compaction.enabled` (defaulting to `true`), but the strict config schema did not accept the key — so there was no way to disable auto-compaction through configuration at all.

## Why This Change Was Made

Of the three options the issue proposed (accept the field, delete the reader, or document the limitation), accepting the field is the only one that makes the existing runtime capability reachable. The boolean is added to the zod schema, `AgentCompactionConfig` type, schema labels/help, and is plumbed into `applyAgentCompactionSettingsFromConfig` as a non-persisted runtime override next to the existing `reserveTokens`/`keepRecentTokens` overrides.

Deliberate boundary: only an explicit `false` is propagated. `true` is already the runtime default, and pushing `true` as a runtime override would outrank `applyAgentAutoCompactionGuard`'s later `setCompactionEnabled(false)` in the settings merge — re-enabling auto-compaction in exactly the silent-overflow cases the guard exists to protect (#75799). A regression test pins this ordering.

## User Impact

Operators can now put `agents.defaults.compaction.enabled: false` in `openclaw.json` to disable auto-compaction (e.g. when an external context engine or provider-side compaction owns it). Configs that set the field no longer fail validation. No behavior change for anyone not setting the field.

target.title: fix: pre-beta.2 state DB upgrade wedges gateway startup and doctor --fix
target.body:
Closes #109867

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users upgrading from `2026.7.2-beta.1` (or any pre-beta.2 state database) would have the gateway fail to start and `openclaw doctor --fix` fail during the shared-state schema migration, leaving the service stranded (reported on macOS LaunchAgent and independently reproduced on Ubuntu systemd in the issue thread).

The failing step is the additive migration for `managed_outgoing_image_records`: it adds `original_media_root` as `TEXT NOT NULL` with no `DEFAULT`. SQLite rejects that `ALTER TABLE … ADD COLUMN` whenever the table has rows — and on older SQLite builds (within OpenClaw's supported Node floor) even when it is empty — so both the startup `ensureSchema` path and the doctor repair path abort with `Cannot add a NOT NULL column with default value NULL`, before the beta.2 index DDL is ever reached.

## Why This Change Was Made

The additive DDL becomes `original_media_root TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ''`, which is executable on every supported SQLite build regardless of table contents, plus the matching `allowedColumnDefinitions` entry in the maintenance schema-compatibility map — the same pattern already used for `current_conversation_bindings.target_agent_id`, whose additive DDL likewise carries a `DEFAULT` the canonical schema omits. The canonical STRICT-table rebuild still normalizes the final shape for databases below the current schema version; no schema-version bump is involved. The empty-string backfill only ever applies to rows written before the column existed (the table had no shipped writer then), and `record_json` remains the durable full record.

## User Impact

Upgrades from pre-beta.2 state databases now complete: the gateway starts normally and `doctor --fix` repairs the schema instead of wedging. Existing rows survive with the new columns backfilled. No behavior change for databases already on the current shape.

## Evidence

Focused test lanes (all green):


target.title: Install ClawHub packages for new Claw agents
target.body:
## Summary

- preflight each exact, version-pinned ClawHub package as install or reuse and bind that owner decision into the consented plan
- revalidate plugin owner state immediately before mutation, then use the existing skill and plugin installer surfaces
- persist pending, complete, or failed package provenance so partial installs and independently owned packages remain explainable
- return structured partial results when a package or later agent/config mutation fails after package work has begun
- warn across CLI, Gateway, and Control UI plugin removal when any Claw provenance, including uncertain provenance, references the plugin

## Scope

This is the package-owner slice of the experimental Claw lifecycle. It keeps the grouped RFC contract (`packages[].kind`, `source`, `ref`, and exact `version`) and deliberately does not restore generic artifact selectors or agent skill lists. MCP servers and cron jobs remain blocked for later stack slices.

The dry-run records whether each package is absent or already present at the exact version. Apply requires the matching plan digest and rechecks plugin owner state before invoking the installer, so a package cannot silently change from Claw-installed to independently owned, or the reverse, after consent. Package work runs before agent/config/workspace mutation; any later collision returns a partial result that retains the package evidence.

Package references describe dependency provenance, not exclusive ownership. An exact package reused from the operator is recorded as independently owned. A Claw-started install is recorded before external mutation and transitions from pending to complete or failed. Existing experimental databases receive the new update timestamp through an additive migration. Plugin uninstall remains operator-controlled but warns for complete and uncertain Claw references.

The CLI remains process-gated by `OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1` in the base of this stack.

target.title: fix(secrets): surface degradation in logs and doctor
target.body:
Related: #101265

## What Problem This Solves

SecretRef degradation can leave one owner cold at startup or keep a stale last-known-good value after reload, but the primary operator signal was easy to miss and could expose low-level resolution text.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Emits a warning-level structured `secrets.degraded` log at startup and reload with redacted owner kind, owner id, reason, cold/stale state, and the `openclaw secrets reload` retry hint.
- Keeps exact owner isolation: a failed webhook route stays cold while unrelated routes remain available.
- Makes doctor list degraded owners with the same redacted reason and retry guidance.
- Attributes typed reload failures to the actual failed owner; an unmapped typed failure reports conservative `unknown:unmapped` / cold metadata without leaking the SecretRef id.

Per maintainer decision, this PR adds no `secrets.degraded[]` gateway protocol/status field, schema, generated Swift model, protocol version bump, config option, parameter, environment variable, UI, or new capability.

## User Impact

Operators get a loud signal in the existing web UI log view and a human-readable doctor section. Public webhook requests remain generic `401 unauthorized`; secret values and SecretRef ids are not logged.

target.title: fix(google-meet): harden talkback bridge recovery
target.body:
Related: #109755, #110089

## What Problem This Solves

PR #110089 landed the three deferred meeting-bot findings while this branch was completing exact-head proof. Sibling-path review found two remaining Google Meet bridge hazards: paired-node talkback could start while microphone state was unknown, and delayed bridge recovery could select another node or open a second tab when tab reuse was disabled.

## Why This Change Was Made

Browser-managed local and paired-node talkback now require an explicit `micMuted: false` observation before realtime audio starts. The explicit externally managed `chrome.launch: false` contract remains unchanged and is documented at its early-return boundary. Delayed bridge recovery pins the session's node and forces the existing-session `chrome.launch: false` path, so it attaches audio without navigating or opening another tab.

## User Impact

Google Meet bots no longer start realtime audio from an unknown microphone state. A paired-node session that becomes speech-ready later keeps its original node and tracked call tab.

## Evidence

- 160 Google Meet integration tests pass, including local and paired-node muted, unknown, unmuted, externally managed, and post-unmute recovery paths.
- 7 Chrome transport tests pass.
- The recovery regression uses `reuseExistingTab: false` and proves `/tabs/open` occurs exactly once.
- Targeted Google Meet lint and `git diff --check` pass.
- Fresh final-delta autoreview: clean, no accepted/actionable findings, patch correct at 0.99 confidence.
- Final exact-head release gate passed all 134 jobs at `b7530205a6ff`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29618128276.

## Maintainer Decision

Unknown microphone state is fail-closed for browser-managed talkback. It remains transiently blocked until Meet explicitly reports `micMuted: false`. Explicit `chrome.launch: false` is the externally managed exception: the external owner supplies the already-open call, so browser health is unavailable and configuring this mode authorizes its bridge directly.

Live signed-in Meet/audio validation was unavailable: connected nodes do not expose the `google-meet` capability, and the approved Meet-capable node is offline. The browser-facing contracts are covered by focused integration tests.

target.title: fix: config rejects compaction.enabled, leaving auto-compaction impossible to disable
target.body:
Closes #110065

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users setting `"enabled": false` under `agents.defaults.compaction` in `openclaw.json` would have their entire config rejected (`agents.defaults.compaction: Invalid input`) when running any gateway command. The session runtime already reads `compaction.enabled` (defaulting to `true`), but the strict config schema did not accept the key — so there was no way to disable auto-compaction through configuration at all.

## Why This Change Was Made

Of the three options the issue proposed (accept the field, delete the reader, or document the limitation), accepting the field is the only one that makes the existing runtime capability reachable. The boolean is added to the zod schema, `AgentCompactionConfig` type, schema labels/help, and is plumbed into `applyAgentCompactionSettingsFromConfig` as a non-persisted runtime override next to the existing `reserveTokens`/`keepRecentTokens` overrides.

Deliberate boundary: only an explicit `false` is propagated. `true` is already the runtime default, and pushing `true` as a runtime override would outrank `applyAgentAutoCompactionGuard`'s later `setCompactionEnabled(false)` in the settings merge — re-enabling auto-compaction in exactly the silent-overflow cases the guard exists to protect (#75799). A regression test pins this ordering.

## User Impact

Operators can now put `agents.defaults.compaction.enabled: false` in `openclaw.json` to disable auto-compaction (e.g. when an external context engine or provider-side compaction owns it). Configs that set the field no longer fail validation. No behavior change for anyone not setting the field.

## Evidence

Targeted test lanes (all green):

```
pnpm vitest run src/config/zod-schema.agent-defaults.test.ts src/agents/agent-settings.test.ts \
  src/config/config.compaction-settings.test.ts src/config/config.schema-regressions.test.ts
 Test Files  5 passed (5)
      Tests  140 passed (140)
```

New tests: schema accepts `enabled: false`/`true` and rejects non-boolean values; `enabled: false` reaches `SettingsManager.getCompactionEnabled()`; explicit `true` does **not** override the auto-compaction guard.

Additionally, a 9-case before/after acceptance matrix was driven through the real `validateConfigObject()` on both `origin/main` and this branch, scored by an external QC harness (Synthia anchor-check panel — objective pass/fail checks only, no LLM judging):

```
  [PASS] bug-reproduced-on-main       main rejects enabled:false with ['agents.defaults.compaction: Unrecognized key: "enabled"']
  [PASS] after/issue-repro-enabled-false     issue #110065 repro: compaction.enabled: false must be accepted
  [PASS] after/enabled-true                  explicit compaction.enabled: true accepted
  [PASS] after/enabled-false-with-siblings   enabled: false composes with existing tuning fields
  [PASS] after/reject-enabled-string         compaction.enabled: "off" (string) must be rejected
  [PASS] after/reject-enabled-number         compaction.enabled: 0 (number) must be rejected
  [PASS] after/reject-enabled-null           compaction.enabled: null must be rejected
  [PASS] after/regression-existing-fields    pre-existing compaction config still accepted unchanged
  [PASS] after/regression-strictness-preserved  unknown compaction keys still rejected (schema stays strict)
  [PASS] after/regression-empty-config       empty config still accepted
  [PASS] no-regression-drift                 pre-existing cases changed acceptance: none

Synthia QC panel: 11/11 checks passed, anchor fidelity 100.0
```

`pnpm check`: typecheck prod/scripts/test-root all pass. The one lint failure (`extensions/qa-lab/src/gateway-child.ts` consistent-return) and one vitest failure (`src/config/sessions/entry-freshness.test.ts`) are pre-existing on `origin/main` (verified in a clean worktree at b7dd330bd3) and untouched by this diff.

**Real CLI behavior proof** (source checkout via `pnpm openclaw`, isolated `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`/`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, scratch paths redacted). The config file contains only `{ "agents": { "defaults": { "compaction": { "enabled": false } } } }`:

```console

$ openclaw config get agents.defaults.compaction
File: <config-path>/openclaw.json
Problem:
  - agents.defaults.compaction: Unrecognized key: "enabled"
Fix: openclaw doctor --fix

# AFTER — this branch, identical config
$ openclaw config validate
Config valid: <config-path>/openclaw.json

$ openclaw config get agents.defaults.compaction
{
  "enabled": false
}

OpenClaw status
(renders the full status table normally; on main this command exits with the validation error above)
```

target.body:
## Summary

- add an experimental core doctor check that projects the canonical Claw lifecycle status model into structured health findings
- report partial installs, missing or modified agents, workspace drift, package drift/incomplete state, MCP ownership drift, unresolved cron ownership, and orphaned subordinate rows
- preserve source MCP placeholders while inspecting runtime config so resolved credentials cannot create false drift
- keep the check and ordered doctor contribution absent unless `OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1`

## Contract

- doctor reuses `claws status` ownership states instead of independently interpreting managed resources
- absent and pre-Claws state produce no findings and no state directory, database, schema, migration, chmod, checkpoint, or journal-mode change
- existing state is observed through one read-only handle; missing experimental ownership tables are treated as empty only in read-only mode
- unreadable, invalid, or forward-version state databases return one structured error finding rather than aborting doctor
- source MCP config is read through the canonical source-config API; `${ENV_VAR}` placeholders remain unexpanded
- diagnostics are advisory and do not mutate config, files, scheduler state, provenance, database bytes, metadata, schema, or journal mode

## Verification

- test-source typecheck
- focused Oxlint: 0 warnings and 0 errors
- formatting and `git diff --check`
- 183 focused lifecycle, collector, shared-state, core-check, and doctor-contribution tests
- absent/pre-Claws tests prove doctor creates no state and changes no bytes
- existing-state test compares database bytes, mtime, mode, `sqlite_master`, `user_version`, and `journal_mode` before and after doctor
- invalid and newer-schema tests prove open failures become structured findings and handles close cleanly
- full Codex review against #102406: no actionable findings

- RFC: https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/27

- This PR: read-only lifecycle and drift diagnostics

target.title: fix(gateway): serialize same-session agent hook dispatches to stop claim-race drops
target.body:
Closes #110109

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators sending multiple near-simultaneous `/hooks/agent` events for the same session (for example a webhook burst: review + inline comments) would silently lose later events when `cron.maxConcurrentRuns > 1`. The first run claimed the session lifecycle lock; losers threw `CronSessionLifecycleClaimError` with no retry, so legitimate automation wakes never ran.

## Why This Change Was Made

Serialize agent-hook runs **per resolved `sessionKey`** at the gateway dispatch boundary: later same-session dispatches chain behind the in-flight run (FIFO), while different session keys stay concurrent. Isolated-agent module load is memoized so concurrent dispatches share one import. This matches the durable fix shape (session-owned queue at hook dispatch) rather than blind pattern retries that can replay side effects after work has started.

Compatibility: no config, protocol, or public API change — only in-process ordering of detached hook work. Performance: different sessions still overlap; idle per-session chains are deleted after the last run. Usability: previously dropped wakes are retained in order. Security: no trust-boundary change; still runs through the existing hook sanitize and system-event paths.

## User Impact

Same-session hook bursts complete in arrival order instead of silently discarding losers. Cross-session concurrency and existing single-hook behavior are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Environment: local macOS openclaw checkout; production `createGatewayHooksRequestHandler` → `dispatchAgentHook` path with mocked `runCronIsolatedAgentTurn` (real dispatch/queue code path).

target.title: fix(cli): exit cleanly on startup migration refusal
target.body:
## Summary

- report the three planned startup migration/config/plugin refusal reasons at their owner, then throw `ExitError(1)` so `ensureConfigReady` uses its existing typed `runtime.exit` path
- add a hermetic child-process regression that exercises a real conflicting plugin-state migration, requires exit status 1 with no signal, verifies the refusal appears exactly once, and confirms the startup migration lease is released
- audit the core `DatabaseSync` migration/checkpoint paths for throw-time handle leaks; every direct handle is already closed by `finally`, so no unrelated migration refactor is included

This PR is stacked on #110200 (base commit `ce6e200aaa2`) because that PR separated the three refusal cases. It should land after #110200.

Refs #109831.

## What Problem This Solves

Startup migration, invalid-config, and plugin-verification refusals were ordinary `Error`s. They bypassed the typed exit handling in `src/cli/program/config-guard.ts`, reached the generic `src/entry.ts` failure handler, and ended in its direct `process.exit(1)` path. In the reported supervised deployment, that path terminated with signal 11 / status 139 instead of a clean refusal status, turning a fail-closed migration result into a supervisor crash loop.

## Root Cause

The proven control-flow mismatch is:

1. `src/commands/doctor-config-preflight.ts` formatted an intentional readiness refusal but threw a plain `Error`.
2. `ensureConfigReady` only converts `ExitError` into `runtime.exit(error.code)`, so it rethrew the refusal.
3. `src/entry.ts` added `Could not start the CLI.` / `Reason:` formatting and called `process.exit(1)`.

The preflight's existing `finally` already releases its heartbeat and startup migration lease before the error leaves the owner. The fix preserves that unwind and hands the intentional refusal to the typed caller contract instead of treating it as an unexpected CLI startup failure.

The reporter's exact native signal source is not established without their core dump. This change fixes the incorrect refusal path and locks down the observable process contract; it does not claim to identify or patch the native module.

## Why This Change Was Made

The refusal owner must print the reason because the typed `ExitError` branch intentionally does not format errors, while the generic entry catch is no longer reached. Printing once immediately before throwing `ExitError(1)` preserves the complete operator guidance without duplicating the generic wrapper.

This is the narrow owner-boundary fix: unexpected preflight errors still use the generic failure handler, and gateway readiness remains fail-closed.

The core migration audit covered the direct `DatabaseSync` constructors in `src/infra/state-migrations.debug-proxy.ts`, `src/infra/state-migrations.task-sidecar-rows.ts`, and `src/infra/state-migrations.storage.ts`, plus the checkpoint database wrapper used by `src/infra/startup-migration-checkpoint.ts`. Each closes in `finally`, including throw paths. No plugin-owned code was changed.

## User Impact

When a startup migration gate refuses readiness, operators retain the full actionable refusal text exactly once. The CLI exits through the typed status-1 path, the migration lease is released, and supervisors see a normal non-zero exit rather than a signal in the covered regression environment.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

The regression creates isolated config/state directories under a realpathed temporary root, seeds conflicting canonical and legacy plugin-state databases, and starts the real TypeScript CLI entry point as a child process:

```text

Test Files  2 passed (2)
Tests       24 passed (24)
Duration    3.29s
```

The child-process assertions observed:

```text

signal: null
refusal reason occurrences on stderr: 1
generic "Could not start the CLI." wrapper occurrences: 0
active startup migration lease after exit: false
```

### Verification

- `pnpm format src/commands/doctor-config-preflight.ts src/commands/doctor-config-preflight.process.test.ts` — passed (`Finished in 6ms on 2 files`)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/doctor-config-preflight.state-migration.test.ts src/commands/doctor-config-preflight.process.test.ts` — 2 files passed, 24 tests passed
- `git diff --check HEAD^ HEAD` — passed

- The reporter's exact container/supervisor/native-module failure was not reproduced; identifying the crashing native module requires the reporter's core dump and is intentionally deferred.

target.body:
## Summary
- scan `~/.omp/agent/sessions/**/*.jsonl` alongside compatible pi session logs
- reuse the existing pi-compatible parser and cache for Codex and Claude attribution
- document OMP support in provider docs, CLI help, and the changelog

Related to #384.

## Redacted runtime proof

I ran the branch against an actual OMP session. The first command reads only metadata and redacts the session filename and token counts:

```console
$ jq '<select first OMP openai-codex assistant message and redact usage>' ~/.omp/agent/sessions/<redacted>.jsonl
{"source":"~/.omp/agent/sessions/<redacted>.jsonl","provider":"openai-codex","api":"openai-codex-responses","model":"gpt-5.6-sol","usage":{"input":"<redacted>","cacheRead":"<redacted>","output":"<redacted>","totalTokens":"<redacted>"}}
```

A fresh local Codex cost scan on the same branch reports that OMP model. Token and cost values are redacted:

```console
$ CodexBarCLI cost --provider codex --format json --refresh --days 1 | jq '<retain source/model and redact usage>'
[
  {
    "provider": "codex",
    "source": "local",
    "daily": [
      {
        "date": "2026-07-17",
        "modelsUsed": ["gpt-5.6-sol"],
        "inputTokens": "<redacted>",
        "cacheReadTokens": "<redacted>",
        "outputTokens": "<redacted>",
        "totalTokens": "<redacted>",
        "totalCost": "<redacted>"
      }
    ]
  }
]
```

## Verification
- `swift test --build-system native --filter 'scanner merges omp sessions with pi sessions'`
- full sharded Swift suite: 696 selections across 58 groups passed (one group passed on the configured retry)
- `make check`
- rebuilt `CodexBarCLI` and ran the redacted runtime proof above against local OMP sessions

The native SwiftPM builder and `DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode-beta.app/Contents/Developer` were used locally because the current macOS 27 command-line toolchain's default builder could not initialize its property-list parser.
